approach: Teach the verbs Spanish uses for size, weight and price (medir, pesar, costar, and tener ... de largo) where English uses "to be" with a number, with the questions to ask and metric units.
coverage: medir (to measure): ¿Cuánto mides? Mido un metro setenta. Mide dos metros.
pesar (to weigh): ¿Cuánto pesa? Pesa cinco kilos.
costar (to cost): ¿Cuánto cuesta? Cuesta diez dólares. Plural: cuestan
Dimensions: tiene tres metros de largo (is three meters long); also de ancho, de alto
English "to be + number" is not ser in Spanish: not Soy un metro setenta
Most Spanish-speaking countries use meters and kilos; US Spanish speakers also use pies, pulgadas and libras
Height is said aloud as un metro setenta (1.70 m)

blocks.purpose: Lays out the three measurement verbs with questions and answers.

data.caption: Size, weight, price

blocks.purpose: States the contrast with English in one rule.

data.anchor: Where English says "is" with a measurement, Spanish uses a verb that names it: mide (measures), pesa (weighs), cuesta (costs).
prerequisites: I am 1.70 m tall: Mido un metro setenta.
It is 3 meters long: Tiene tres metros de largo (or Mide tres metros de largo).
Medir changes e to i (mido, mides, mide); costar changes o to ue (cuesta, cuestan).

blocks.purpose: Targets translating "I am 1.70 m" with soy.

data.question: How do you say "I am 1.65 m tall"?
choices: Mido un metro sesenta y cinco.
Soy un metro sesenta y cinco.
Estoy un metro sesenta y cinco.
Tengo un metro sesenta y cinco.

trapReasons.1: English says "I am ... tall", and soy means "I am".

data.whyIntuitionFailed: English uses "to be" for height, so learners reach for soy.
data.correctReasoning: Spanish measures height with medir: Mido un metro sesenta y cinco. (Soy alto, "I am tall", is fine without a number.)
data.recoveryTip: A number of meters: mido. A description: soy alto.

data.takeaway: Mide for height and length, pesa for weight, cuesta and cuestan for price: Spanish names the measurement instead of saying "is".

checks.prompt: Which sentence says "The baby weighs four kilos"?
checks.rationale: Weight uses pesar: pesa cuatro kilos. Mide is for height or length, and cuesta for price.

checks.prompt: In a store you point at two shirts. Which question asks their price?
checks.rationale: Price uses costar, and two shirts are plural: cuestan.

checks.prompt: Complete with one word: "Yo ___ un metro setenta." (I am 1.70 m tall.)
checks.rationale: Height in numbers uses medir, and the yo form is mido.
